summary: Learn to use student success analytics to predict risk, target support, and improve retention.
lede: Student support, retention and success analytics helps institutions turn engagement, performance, and support data into targeted actions that keep learners progressing and completing on time. Over five days, you will define retention KPIs, build early-alert indicators and risk profiles, and connect support interventions to measurable outcomes. You will work hands-on with real or sample data to create dashboards, scorecards, triage rules, support journeys, and intervention plans using spreadsheet-based analytics and tools such as Power BI or Tableau. The course also introduces predictive modeling and AI-assisted risk scoring conceptually, helping you build a practical analytics system despite fragmented data, limited analyst capacity, and competing priorities.
audienceIntro: This course is built for education professionals who use data to design, deliver, and improve student support and retention initiatives across programs and delivery modes.
modules: Data Readiness and Governance for Student Success
Designing Early-Alert Indicators and Risk Signals
Dashboards for Student Support and Retention
Linking Analytics to Student Support Interventions
Designing a Student Success Analytics Operating Model
prerequisites: This is an intermediate-level course suitable for professionals with basic experience in student support, institutional research, or education data. You should be comfortable working with spreadsheets, interpreting basic statistics such as percentages and trends, and reading simple dashboards. No coding is required; all hands-on activities use tools such as Excel, Power BI, or Tableau at a configuration and interpretation level, not programming. Experience with a learning management system and a student information system is strongly recommended so you can relate exercises to your own context. If you bring anonymized sample data from your institution, you will be able to tailor the exercises more directly to your reality.
